analysis: The supplied units are lines 1-1219 of StandaloneServer.swift (head). The only changed hunk, in the patch at head lines ~1538-1564, falls outside both units. It adds a one-time `releaseReclaimableMemoryForLoad()` call, run before LRU eviction in the memory-headroom wait loop. That call runs `GlobalKVCacheBudget.releaseRetainedKVSegments()` and, if `nativeMiMoReclaimAllowed`, `MLX.Memory.clearCache()`. It is guarded by `poolDropped`, so it runs at most once per call. It also keeps the native MiMo reclaim gate, matching the other `clearCache` call sites in finishShutdown (lines 726-733) and the release/clear path in resliceAndBuildBundle (line 1181). It does not weaken the load-gate serialization, KV grant accounting or auth. It drops only cached free buffers and retained free KV segments, which reduces residual GPU data (T-028) rather than adding exposure. Relevance to T-041 is limited: the prefix-cache SSD tier, the DBK3 crypto, the HMAC lookup tags, the TTL and the scope derivation are untouched. The change is standalone local mode only (no coordinator or provider wire boundary). Within the visible units I found no authorization, attestation, encryption or billing regression. Unverified: the implementation of `GlobalKVCacheBudget.releaseRetainedKVSegments` and `busyEnginesKeepReclaimableMemory` (including its 'waits briefly' behavior and any lock or actor interaction with the load gate) is not in the supplied evidence. Its availability or deadlock impact, and whether the release is unsafe for in-flight engines, cannot be assessed. The changed hunk lines themselves are not shown as numbered text. I therefore cannot cite them, and that part is only partially reviewed.
